headline: Bond vol finally broke — and the bounce went to the roadkill, not the leaders, which is the first honest rotation in a month.
summary: The rates shock took its first real hit. MOVE fell 8.2% to 96.00, the first meaningful break after a month in which it rose 38.3% (z=2.07). The 2-year dropped 6bp to 4.81% and the 5-year 5bp to 4.98%, and 2s10s steepened 5bp to 36bp. Brent fell another 8.6% to $97.47 — down 6.2% on the week — and RBOB gasoline fell 10.3%, now -9.4% in five sessions. Breakevens are inert: 5-year at 2.34% is up only 3bp in a month (z=0.10). The inflation composite improved to -38 from -40, rates to -76 from -80, risk regime to -10 from -12. That is relief, not a turn.

Why it isn't a turn: the long end refused to play. The 30-year rose 2bp to 5.49%, sitting at the 100th percentile of the past year; the 10-year is 5.17% and the 10-year real yield 2.83%, up 49bp in a month (z=1.94). TLT is at an outright 52-week low (pos52=0.0), IEF at the 5th percentile, LQD at the 1st. The 30-year mortgage is 7.03%, a 52-week high. And the 3-month bill at 4.24% is up 39bp in a month with acceleration z=1.84, also at the 100th percentile. So today's rally was the belly, not the wings — the curve bear-steepened. The bond market is pricing a Fed that cannot cut and a term premium that will not compress, and the equity market still discounts neither.

Inside equities, the character of the tape changed for one day. The Dow rose 0.9% against the S&P's 0.5%; FDX +2.3%, UPS +2.1%, CAT +2.0%, COST +2.9%, JETS +1.8%, XHB +1.6%, ITB +1.3%, KRE and KBE +0.9% each. The leaders wobbled: META -3.3% after a +30.6% month (z=2.47), ORCL -1.7% and now -52.4% year-on-year at the 11th percentile, COIN -2.1%, software/semis -2.0%. But one session fixes nothing. RSP/SPY is still -5.5% on the month at z=-2.61, IWM/SPY fell another 0.4% today and is -6.3% on the month, and IYT/SPY remains pinned at its absolute 52-week low. Read today as an oil-driven short cover in the most fuel- and rate-levered names, not a breadth repair — the repair needs the 30-year to stop rising.

Cross-asset confirms growth, not easing. Copper rose 0.9% to 6.779, the 98.8th percentile; copper/gold is +10.7% in a month with acceleration z=1.97; XLI/XLU is at a 52-week high. Growth pulse +17. The dollar eased 0.3% to 101.04 but the monthly trend is +1.9% with acceleration 1.6, USDCHF is at a 52-week high and USDMXN rose another 0.8% (+4.3% on the month, acc z=1.78) — the EM FX squeeze is the one stress that accelerated today. Precious metals logged a second stabilization day: silver +2.0%, platinum +3.0%, GDXJ +1.1%, after acceleration prints of -3.2 in gold and -3.12 in GDX. And VIX closed 14.87, 8th percentile, credit & vol composite +46 against rates -76. That gap narrowed today. It is still the biggest unreconciled spread on the board.

good.text: Bond volatility cracked: MOVE -8.2% to 96.00 after a +38.3% month, with the 2-year -6bp to 4.81% and the 5-year -5bp to 4.98%. First genuine easing of the rates shock; rates composite improved to -76 from -80.
The oil unwind extended: Brent -8.6% to $97.47 (-6.2% week), RBOB -10.3% (-9.4% week), WTI -2.3%. Breakevens confirm no inflation impulse — 5y at 2.34%, +3bp in a month; inflation composite -38.

Beaten-up cyclicals were bid hardest: FDX +2.3%, UPS +2.1%, CAT +2.0%, COST +2.9%, JETS +1.8%, XHB +1.6%, KRE +0.9%, Dow +0.9% vs S&P +0.5%. Lowest-quality tape leadership rotating toward the cheapest names.
Growth signal intact: copper +0.9% at the 98.8th percentile, copper/gold +10.7% on the month with acceleration z=1.97, XLI/XLU at a 52-week high. Growth pulse composite +17.
Asia tech keeps leading: EWY +2.5%, EWJ +2.2%, EWT +1.5%, Nikkei +1.3%, SOXX +1.2% (+11.2% on the month), MSFT +3.7%. SMH/SPY z=1.02 with positive acceleration.
Precious metals stabilized a second day after statistical capitulation: silver +2.0%, platinum +3.0%, GDXJ +1.1%, gold +0.5% — against monthly acceleration z of -3.2 in gold and -3.12 in GDX.

bad.text: The long end still won't quit: 30-year +2bp to 5.49% at the 100th percentile, 10-year real yield 2.83% (+49bp in a month, z=1.94), 30-year mortgage 7.03% at a 52-week high. TLT at a 52-week low, IEF 5th percentile, LQD 1st percentile.
Breadth did not improve despite the rotation: RSP/SPY -5.5% on the month at z=-2.61, IWM/SPY -0.4% today and -6.3% on the month, transports/S&P still at its absolute 52-week low.
Front-end easing is being priced out, not in: 3-month bill 4.24%, +39bp in a month, acceleration z=1.84, 100th percentile. The belly rallied; the bill did not move.

Dollar squeeze accelerating against EM and commodity FX: USDMXN +0.8% (+4.3% month, acc z=1.78), USDCHF at a 52-week high, USDCAD +2.2% on the month, AUDJPY -3.2% and rolling over. DXY acceleration z=1.6 despite today's 0.3% dip.

Leadership cracked at the top: META -3.3% after a +30.6% month (z=2.47), ORCL -1.7% and -52.4% y/y at the 11th percentile, COIN -2.1%, software/semis -2.0%. When nine stocks are the index, that is where risk lives.

Consumer and power complexes remain in liquidation: MCD at a 52-week low (-10.8% month, z=-2.32), HD 1st percentile, NKE 0.7th, XRT/SPY 0.7th; NLR -14.5% (z=-2.1), URA -14.9%, REMX -14.6%, XLU at the 2nd percentile.

trades.name: 2s30s bear steepener
trades.line: Steepener: long 2y futures vs short ultra-bond
trades.expr: Long TU (2y) futures vs short WN (ultra-bond) DV01-neutral, or buy a 2s30s steepener via swaps; retail proxy long SHY vs short TLT.
trades.thesis: The rates shock is bifurcating. The Fed path can finally soften as oil collapses, but term premium and supply own the long end. 2s10s at 36bp is in the 30th percentile of the last year with the 30-year at the 100th — that is not a stable combination.
trades.trigger: 2-year -6bp to 4.81% and 5-year -5bp while the 30-year rose 2bp to 5.49%; 2s10s +5bp today, +11bp on the week; MOVE -8.2% to 96.00 as the front end led the rally.
trades.stop: 2s10s back through 25bp, or the 3-month bill making another leg above 4.35% (acc z already 1.84) as the market re-prices hikes and flattens the curve.
trades.target: 2s10s to 65-75bp, back toward the top of the 3-month range; 3m10y is already at 93bp and the 93rd percentile.

trades.name: Equity vol vs a 5.17% 10-year
trades.line: Buy SPX/SPY downside; VIX 14.87 at the 8th percentile
trades.expr: Buy Nov/Dec SPY 5-7% OTM put spreads funded by selling 10% OTM puts, or VIX Nov 18/25 call spreads. Size 50-75bp premium.
trades.thesis: Equity vol is priced for a benign world that the bond market does not endorse: credit & vol composite +46 versus rates -76. With the S&P at the 96th percentile and equal-weight breadth 2.6 sigma weak, index vol is the cheapest hedge against the narrowing.
trades.trigger: VIX -5.1% to 14.87 (8th percentile) and VIX3M 17.93 (4th percentile) on a day the 30-year rose and META fell 3.3%; SKEW turning up at 144.91 with RSP/SPY z=-2.61.
trades.stop: VIX term structure inverting is the confirmation, not the stop — cut if VIX3M breaks below 16 with RSP/SPY reclaiming its 200-day (ext currently -4.05%).
trades.target: VIX 22-25, roughly the level that accompanied the last 5% S&P drawdown; SPY 5-7% lower.

trades.name: Transports vs S&P on the fuel crash
trades.line: Long IYT vs short SPY: fuel down 9%, ratio at 52wk low
trades.expr: Long IYT (or XTN for equal-weight), short an equivalent notional of SPY. 1:1 dollar-neutral.
trades.thesis: Transports discount recession while their single biggest variable cost just collapsed. IYT/SPY is at the absolute 52-week low with a z-score of -2.63 — a two-sigma-plus dislocation into a 9.4% weekly drop in gasoline and a 6.2% fall in Brent.
trades.trigger: FDX +2.3% and UPS +2.1% today after -14.6% and -11.1% monthly drawdowns; JETS +1.8%; IYT +0.5% with the ratio stabilizing for the first time in a month.
trades.stop: IYT/SPY making a new low below today's level, or Brent reclaiming $105 — the fuel relief is the entire thesis.
trades.target: IYT/SPY back to its 200-day, currently 1.9% above spot, then the 3-month mean — roughly 8-10% of relative performance.

trades.name: Gold miners capitulation reversal
trades.line: Long GDXJ: acceleration z=-2.75 with metal turning up
trades.expr: Long GDXJ outright, or long GDX Dec call spreads. Add on a gold close back above its 200-day (currently 5.2% above spot).
trades.thesis: The metals drawdown was statistical, not fundamental: gold -7.2% in a month with acceleration z=-3.2, GDX -3.12, NEM -3.2. Those are washout readings, and the miners' 3-month relative strength versus the S&P is still +13.7%. A stabilizing 10-year real yield removes the proximate cause of the selling.
trades.trigger: Second consecutive up day in the complex — silver +2.0%, platinum +3.0%, GDXJ +1.1%, gold +0.5% — with GDXJ flipping to turning_up and the 10-year real yield down 2bp.
trades.stop: Gold closing below 4,150 (roughly 4% under spot), or GDX/gold breaking its 200-day, which sits 8.2% below the current ratio.
trades.target: GDXJ +12-15%, retracing half of the 8.8% monthly decline plus the miner beta; gold back toward its 200-day.

trades.name: Homebuilders into a 7.03% mortgage
trades.line: Short XHB/ITB on the bounce; mortgage at 52wk high
trades.expr: Short ITB or buy Dec XHB puts ~7% OTM. Fade strength; do not chase weakness.
trades.thesis: Housing has no relief because the relief happened in the belly, not the long end. The 30-year mortgage at 7.03% is a 52-week high and tracks the 10-year, which fell just 1bp today while the 30-year Treasury rose. XHB/SPY is in the 4th percentile and trending down.
trades.trigger: XHB +1.6% and ITB +1.3% today, +2.6%/+2.3% on the week — a bounce in a tape where the 30-year yield is at the 100th percentile and DHI is -14.6% over three months.
trades.stop: The 10-year breaking back below 4.90% (it is 16.8% above its 200-day), or XHB reclaiming its 200-day, currently 6.9% above spot.
trades.target: ITB retest of the September lows, another 8-10% lower; XHB/SPY into new 52-week low territory.

trades.name: BX as the private-credit canary
trades.line: Short BX: -17.3% in a month while the S&P sits at highs
trades.expr: Short BX outright or buy Jan puts; hedge with a long in XLF if you want sector-neutral.
trades.thesis: The alternative managers are where a 4.98% five-year and a 52-week-low IG bond market actually bite: marks, fundraising and realization fees all compress. BX is down 17.3% on the month (z=-1.81) with acceleration -1.61 while the index made highs — that divergence usually resolves in the stock's direction.
trades.trigger: LQD at the 1st percentile of the last year (-2.9% on the month), HYG rolling over at z=-1.33, IAI -7.0% and KIE -6.6% on the month, and BX bouncing only 1.0% on a broad financials up day.
trades.stop: BX reclaiming its 200-day, currently 7.0% above spot, or IG credit rallying with LQD back above its 200-day.
trades.target: BX 12-15% lower toward the 2025 lows; watch HYG/IEF rolling over as confirmation the credit channel is opening.

trades.name: Long USD vs MXN
trades.line: Long USDMXN: acc z=1.78 while EM equities ignore it
trades.expr: Long USD/MXN spot or 3-month forwards; alternatively buy 3-month USDMXN calls struck near 18.25.
trades.thesis: The peso is the carry trade most exposed to a re-firming dollar and a collapsing oil price. USDMXN is +4.3% in a month with acceleration z=1.78 while EEM rose 1.1% today — EM equity is not yet discounting what EM FX is saying, and that gap tends to close toward the currency.
trades.trigger: USDMXN +0.8% today and +3.0% on the week to 17.676 on a day the DXY actually fell 0.3%; USDCHF at a 52-week high and CEW -1.4% on the month.
trades.stop: USDMXN back below 17.20, or the 3-month bill breaking lower as the Fed path re-softens and the dollar trend (acc z=1.6) rolls.
trades.target: 18.50, the top of the 12-month range; EWW/MXX underperformance is the equity confirmation.
